name: V1162 Aql
description: A Cepheid in the Milky Way that pulsates every 5.38 days; its mean radius is 42.7 solar radii.

radius.source: Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10, V1162 Aql: Baade-Wesselink mean radius (solar radii) 42.7 +/- 10.9 (Monte-Carlo)

temperature.source: Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, VizieR J/A+A/635/A33/table1, recno 202, Name='V1162 Aql', columns Teff, e_Teff (K): Teff 5625 +/- 168 K from a fit to the spectral energy distribution at mean light (not spectroscopic)

distance.source: Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10, V1162 Aql: Baade-Wesselink distance (pc) 1249.2 +/- 305.1 (Monte-Carlo)

color.reason: Interstellar dust reddens every spectrum of this star, E(B-V) = 0.205 +/- 0.021 (Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10), and its light changes through each pulsation

text.card: A Cepheid in the Milky Way, 43 times the Sun's width, that swells and shrinks every 5.4 days.
text.introduction: Its mean radius, 42.7 solar radii, comes from comparing how fast its surface moves with how its size changes, 1,249 parsecs away.
text.locator: table10, V1162 Aql: Per, Rad, Dist

notes: The star pulsates; it is drawn at its mean radius.
No dynamical mass is measured for this Cepheid; its mass is left unmeasured.
